title: Contracting under Misspecification
abstract: arXiv:2609.25590v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper studies agency problems when both parties worry that the model linking action to output is misspecified. With observable actions, an optimal contract is linear in output, so performance pay arises solely to share misspecification exposure, the slope reflects the parties' relative robustness concerns, and its allocation is Pareto efficient. With hidden actions, this sharing rule survives and incentives add a nonlinear correction. Misspecification concerns can polarize effort by making intermediate actions impossible to implement. Moreover, ambiguity across competing models has asymmetric effects: uncertainty about desired actions raises the principal's payoff, whereas uncertainty about deviations can lower it.

translated_title: 模型误设下的契约设计
translated_abstract: 本文研究当委托代理双方都担心连接行动与产出的模型存在误设时的代理问题。在行动可观察的情况下，最优契约对产出是线性的，因此绩效薪酬的产生仅仅是为了分担模型误设的风险敞口，其斜率反映了双方相对的稳健性担忧程度，且这种风险分担的配置是帕累托有效的。在行动隐藏（不可观察）的情况下，这一风险分担规则依然成立，而激励则表现为一个非线性修正项。对模型误设的担忧可能通过使中间水平的行动无法实施而导致努力程度两极分化。此外，不同竞争模型之间的模糊性具有不对称的影响：对期望行动的不确定性会提高委托人的收益，而对偏离行动的不确定性则可能降低委托人的收益。
tldr: 该论文在双方均担心模型误设的委托代理框架下证明，最优契约为产出的线性函数，绩效薪酬的作用仅在于分担模型误设风险，隐藏行动时激励仅表现为非线性修正，且模型模糊性对委托人收益具有不对称影响。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that when both parties worry about model misspecification, the optimal contract is linear in output—with performance pay serving solely to share misspecification exposure—hidden-action incentives add only a nonlinear correction, and ambiguity across competing models has asymmetric effects on the principal's payoff.
